newsitem.title: USA: IBM jumps at open, some profit-taking seen.
newsitem.headline: IBM jumps at open, some profit-taking seen.

text.p: Shares in International Business Machines Corp. leaped $12.125 to $154.50 Thursday in response to its favorable earnings report.

The stock jumped in response to its better-than-expected earnings per share of $2.37 a share, which was well above the consensus Wall Street estimate for $2.28 a share. IBM reported its first quarter results after the close of trading Wednesday.

The surge in IBM's stock contributed to a strong opening for the Dow Jones industrial average, which gained as much as 78 points to 6,891 in early trading. The Dow Jones industrial average subsequently retreated as some profit taking developed in blue chips, including IBM.

Analysts and traders said IBM's better than expected earnings were a big relief to Wall Street, especially after rumours circulated a few weeks ago that the computer giant would not meet analysts' estimates.
Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons said IBM was adding more than 34 points to the Dow.

"It is directly helping the Dow and indirectly lifting the high tech sector," Goldman said. "It's making people feel much better for the moment. People are saying 'Gee, the economy is stronger than we thought. Earnings will be climbing'."
